title: Investigation deck for stochastic latency sources
content:
Executive summary:

This is a working investigation deck to surface repeatable heuristics and lightweight instrumentation changes for diagnosing stochastic / bursty latency observed in tokenized inference paths. The objective: reduce time-to-root-cause from on-call -> triage -> owner to < 45 minutes for common patterns (KV cold tails, noisy tenants, scheduling jitter).

Intended audience: oncall operators, SREs, serving-runtime engineers, product owners running rollouts.

Phenomenology (how these outages look in practice):
- Quantile blips: 99th/99.9th moving up while p50/p95 hold steady.
- Multi-modal latency distribution: a tight fast path plus sparse high outliers.
- Correlated error/latency: elevated retried RPCs or transient model fallback.
- Tenant-local pockets: single tenant or small tenant cohort showing large delta vs global median.

Common hypotheses (quick check order):
1) Cold KV / prefix not cached -> first request penalty, often correlated with host-level memory pressure.
2) Scheduling preemption or GPU context switching -> host-level CPU steal / cgroup throttling signals.
3) Tracing sampling bias: missing long tails because sampling dropped those spans.
4) Downstream RPC retries -> dependency latency multiplier.
5) Burst-induced batching timeouts -> adaptive batching waits for micro-batches causing jitter.

Metric definitions (what to instrument / name guidance):
- request.latency.ms: histogram (buckets: 1,2,5,10,25,50,100,250,500,1000,2500). Tag keys: model, tenant_id, route, batch_size, kv_read_hit (true|false).
- kv.lookup.latency.ms: histogram (same buckets). Tags: backend (redis/rocks), key_shard, result_size, hot_prefix (bool).
- scheduling.cpu.steal.percent: gauge per host.
- gpu.context.switch.count: counter per GPU device over 1s windows.
- dependency.rpc.retry.rate: counter (per downstream id).
- batch.wait.ms: histogram by route and configured max_wait_ms.
- trace.sampled: counter; trace.sampled.long_tail.counter (tagged by sample_decision_reason).

Trace/Span design suggestions (minimally invasive):
- Add a lightweight span at the start/end of: request routing, kv lookup, model enqueue, model decode. Keep these spans < 2 tags to avoid cardinality explosion.
- Use standardized span names: span.request.route, span.kv.lookup, span.model.enqueue, span.model.decode.
- Annotate spans with boolean hot_cache_hint when warm-path heuristics apply.
- Prefer sparse high-fidelity traces: emit full payloads only when latency > p99 OR when kv_lookup_miss=true.
- Trace-sampling policy: always sample: (a) 1 in 100 requests globally, (b) 100% of requests with latency > p99 and/or kv_lookup_miss=true, (c) 1 in 10 for tenants flagged as noisy.

Dashboard layout proposals (compact operator-first):
Top row: signal overview (global p50/p95/p99, request rate, error rate) with quick tenant selector.
Second row: tail-attribution tiles (p99 by tenant, p99 by model, p99 by host).
Third row: path decomposition small-multiples (request.latency.ms histogram split by kv_read_hit true/false; batch.wait.ms; dependency.rpc.latency).
Fourth row: host health (cpu.steal, memory_pressure, disk_io_wait) + GPU context switches.
Right rail: live trace sampling counts, recent long-tail traces list (link to trace ids).

Compact investigation runbook (operator checklist):
1) Narrow time window to the latency spike, note affected routes/tenants.
2) Open p99-by-tenant tile; if single tenant -> tag and escalate to solutions-eng as tenant-noise.
3) Check kv.lookup.latency.ms + kv.hit-rate. If hit-rate dropped -> mark cold-cache hypothesis.
4) Inspect batch.wait.ms. If median > configured max_wait -> batching-induced tail.
5) Cross-check host-level cpu.steal and gpu.context.switch. If elevated -> scheduling/preemption.
6) Pull 3 sampled traces from the window (prefer latency > p99) and inspect span timing order.
7) If dependency retry rate jumps -> drill into downstream dependency dashboards and owner.
8) Capture hypothesis and short-term mitigation (scale more workers, increase kv replica, lower max_wait_ms) in incident notes.

Experiment matrix (small changes to try):
- KV TTL/replica experiment: 10% traffic -> increase prefetch/populate to reduce cold misses; measure p99 and qps cost.
- Batching timeout change: reduce max_wait_ms for one model route by 50% for 5% of traffic and monitor p50/p99 and effective throughput.
- Trace sampling tweak: 100% sample for bucket of traffic for 1h during quiet period, to collect more tail traces for hypothesis building.
- Tenant shaping trial: temporally throttle bursts from noisy tenant to see system-wide tail reductions.

Low-cardinality tagging strategy (avoid explosion):
- Do tag on tenant_id only when investigating; otherwise use tenant_cohort (small set: heavy, medium, light).
- Model tag: use model_family (e.g., gptx-13b, llama-2-70b) not full version; surface version in trace payloads for sampled traces.

Ownership & rollout guardrails:
- Any instrumentation that adds tags must include a toy-cost estimate (metric cardinality multiplier).
- Roll experimental sampling/routing changes behind feature flags and a canary traffic % (1%, 10%, 100%).

Open questions / unknowns to surface to the research backlog:
- Can we detect cold-kv rises pre-emptively via synthetic probe correlated to tenant cohort?
- Is GPU context-switch count correlated with specific cloud instance types or underlying hypervisor configurations?
- How to unify batch-level vs token-level latency attribution in a single trace without creating massive spans?

Immediate next steps (this week):
- [ ] Patch runtime to emit span.model.enqueue and span.model.decode with hot_cache_hint tag (owner: serving-runtime, PR: GH-PR-2147).
- [ ] Add p99-by-tenant tile (owner: obs-dashboard, ticket: JIRA-OBS-1172).
- [ ] Implement trace-sampling policy rollout plan: canary 1% -> 10% -> 100% for high-latency sampling (owner: eng-observability).

Notes to self / friction points:
- Keep metric names stable; we should avoid introducing multiple synonymous metrics during this investigation.
- Watch for query cost on dashboards when adding fine-grained splits. Add cached snapshot panels for heavy queries.

Appendix: quick SQL snippets (pseudo) for operators
- p99-by-tenant: SELECT tenant_cohort, approx_percentile(latency_ms,0.99) FROM requests WHERE ts BETWEEN t0 AND t1 GROUP BY tenant_cohort
- kv-miss-list: SELECT tenant_id, count(*) as misses FROM kv_events WHERE result='miss' AND ts BETWEEN t0 AND t1 GROUP BY tenant_id ORDER BY misses DESC LIMIT 50

End of deck.

Feedback welcome — this is meant to be an actionable working-source to fold into onboarding for oncall and into the rollout playbook for model releases.
